[i][b]{Conversation. . . . .}
[/b][/i]

Characters:

- Vadim "The Shevardnadze" Mirovich  A cunning oligarch, controlling arms trade and black-market finance. 

- Sergei "Iron Hand" Volkov  A brutal ex-military commander turned mafia warlord, overseeing Sikirsks mercenary forces. He wears a thick leather trench coat, a pistol holstered at his side.

Location: Yugorsk - Capital of Sikirsk

Vadim Mirovich: (staring out the window, watching the snowfall over the dark city)
"Yugorsk in winter. Cold, quiet, almost peaceful If you dont know where to look."

Sergei Volkov: (grunts, setting his gloves on the table and rubbing his hands by the fire)
"Peace is an illusion. The real business happens in the dark. Deals made in the back rooms, bodies left in alleyways. Snow just covers the blood until spring."

Vadim Mirovich: (smirks, taking a sip of vodka, the glass fogging slightly in his hand)
"Speaking of bloodErenes turning red. Our contractors are getting sloppy. Too many bodies, too many whispers. The local enforcers are starting to poke around."

Sergei Volkov: (lights a cigar, the glow reflecting in his cold eyes)
"Let them poke. Fear makes men cautious. And cautious men pay for protection. The trick is making them afraid enough to buy our silence, but not brave enough to try and stop us."

Vadim Mirovich: (chuckles, shaking his head)
"A fine balance, my friend. One we've mastered."

(He gestures to the window, where below, armored SUVs move through the icy streets, flanked by armed men. The mercenary army, their soldiers blending into the night, moving unseen between the city's shadows.)

Sergei Volkov: (exhales smoke, watching the scene below)
"This city is ours, Vadim. And yet some fools forget that. The smaller mates in the Echelon Collective are restless. They think we take too much, leave them scraps. They whisper about breaking away."

Vadim Mirovich: (slowly turns to face Sergei, his smirk fading into something colder)
"Then lets remind them what happens to traitors in winter."

Sergei Volkov: (grins, showing his gold tooth)
"Ill arrange a demonstration. A few disappearances. A few 'accidents' on the icy roads. The rest will fall in line."

(They clink glasses, the fire crackling behind them, while outside, the mercenary army moves through the frozen nightsilent, unseen, unstoppable.)
